title: G47: PBMCs of Diabetic subject without DFU
extract_protocol_ch1: Skin biopsies were kept in sterile PBS on ice until processing, normally within a few hours post-surgery. The skin was cleaned by sequentially immersing in 10% Betadine, 70% ethanol and PBS for 1 minute at a time. Then it was incubated in 5 mg/ml Dispase II (Thermo Fisher) in HBSS (STEMCELL) overnight at 4°C. The next day, the epidermis was peeled off using forceps and the tissue was finely minced with a No. 10 disposable scalpel. The skin pieces were then placed in an enzyme cocktail consisting of 3.3 mg/ml Collagenase-P (Roche), 3.3 mg/ml Dispase II and 1.5 mg/ml DNase I in 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA, and incubated for 90 minutes at 37°C with constant shaking, using glass pipettes for trituration every 20 min. Enzymes were then inactivated with addition of complete DMEM (+10%FBS, +1% Pen/Strep). The single cell suspension was passed through 70 um and 40 um cell strainers and centrifuged 10min, 500g at 4°C. For RBC lysis ACK buffer (Lonza) was added.

Library preparation was performed using the Chromium 3’V2 and 3 reagent kits (10X genomics). Gel bead-in-emulsions (GEMs) were generated, and bar coded by loading single cell suspensions in Single cell chip B along with gel beads and reverse transcription (RT) master mix and running on the 10X genomics chromium controller. Following RT, the cDNA was amplified and used to generate 3’ libraries. The libraries were quantified using Qubit 3.0 fluorometer, and quality was assessed using HS DNA chips with 2100 Bioanalyzer (Agilent technologies). Sequencing was performed using massively parallel sequencing on the Novaseq S4 instrument (Illumina).
